prompt: Implement a directed graph whose node labels are any type bounded by Comparable, supporting sorted node listing, a deterministic breadth-first shortest path, and cycle detection. Complete LabeledGraph in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The bound T extends Comparable<T> is what lets the adjacency lists live in a TreeMap of TreeSets, and that ordering is exactly what makes the results reproducible: duplicate edges collapse, nodesSorted is just the key set, and breadth-first search visits neighbours smallest-first. Shortest path is BFS with a cameFrom map, walked backwards from the target and reversed -- recording the predecessor only the first time a node is seen is what keeps the tie-break honest. Cycle detection is a depth-first search that marks nodes currently on the recursion stack; meeting such a node again means a cycle, while a node already finished is merely a revisit.
hints: Store the graph as a Map<T, TreeSet<T>> from each node to its out-neighbours, and make sure addEdge creates an entry for the destination too so it shows up in nodesSorted.
For shortestPath use a queue plus a Map<T, T> recording who discovered each node. Only set that entry the first time a node is seen; then follow it back from the target and reverse the list.
For hasCycle keep two sets: nodes fully finished, and nodes currently on the recursion stack. Reaching a node that is on the stack is a cycle; reaching a finished node is not.
